claim: Greenland and Antarctica hold over 68% of Earth's fresh water; fully melted, Greenland would raise sea level about 7.4 m (24 ft) and Antarctica about 58 m (190 ft).

beats.caption: Earth has just two ice sheets.
beats.vo: Earth has just two ice sheets: Greenland and Antarctica. Together they hold over two-thirds of all the fresh water on Earth.

beats.caption: Greenland: about 24 feet
beats.vo: Melt all of Greenland, and the sea would rise about 24 feet.

beats.caption: Antarctica: about 190 feet
beats.vo: Melt all of Antarctica, and it's about 190 feet. It's far bigger: over five million square miles, and up to three miles thick.

beats.caption: Extreme case, not a forecast.
beats.vo: That's the extreme case, not a forecast. But both ice sheets are already losing ice, and it's already raising sea levels. Which coastline would you check first?

sources.text: NSIDC, Ice Sheets: https://nsidc.org/learn/parts-cryosphere/ice-sheets (68% of fresh water; Greenland 7.4 m / 24 ft; Antarctica 58 m / 190 ft; Antarctic area ~14 million km2 / 5.4 million mi2, up to ~4.9 km / 3 mi thick)
